ecus.notes: Sport 1100, V10 Centauro and Daytona RS. This controller uses Marelli's pre-KWP echoed one-byte diagnostic protocol, not ISO 14230 frames. The physical initialization and register layout are corroborated by a field capture/open implementation for the IAW 1.6M family, the published Marelli 16F protocol, IAW Scan 2's independent 16F implementation, and ScanST's tested Moto Guzzi 16M support. Temperature conversion differs between the 16F publication (-40 C) and the recovered 1.6M implementation (-55 C), so the workstation deliberately exposes those channels as raw counts. Active-test bytes, clear-errors and reset bytes are known but intentionally unavailable: they are ECU-timed single-byte commands and do not fit the workstation's explicit on/off safety contract.

memory.hardware_note: Readable on the bench: 12V on pins 4 and 17, ground on 10 and 34, K-Line on pin 16. Use a battery tender if the ECU is still on the bike.

flash.note: 0x4000-0x50000. The bootloader below 0x4000 is not reachable over K-Line. Observed directly in a 5AM HW610 dump.

eeprom.note: Holds the learned values: TPS zero, CO trim, fault memory, immobilizer codes. IAW5AMEEPROMTool covers this; the region geometry has not been captured here, so size is unset and reads will refuse rather than guess.

security.note: Seed is a 16-bit value X followed by X+1. Algorithm transcribed from 5am_util main.c calc_key() and registered as iaw5am-kwp-divmod (unverified on Guzzi hardware). See docs/PRIOR_ART.md 1.1.

session.note: 10 85 03 switches the ECU to the programming session and the line to 38400; AccessTimingParameter sets P2/P3/P4. Unlike the read path there is no 10 0C session, and the tester address stays 0xF1 (except the 27 exchange, which 5am_util sends from 0x01).

records.note: Writer identification. GuzziDiag's writer sends its TesterCode here; 5am_util sends it empty. Mandatory: RequestDownload fails without a 0x3B 98 20 record.
Reflash date, YY MM DD. 5am_util sends 2018-01-01.

erase.note: 31 02 arms the erase for 0x4000..0x4FFFF; 33 02 is what makes it run. The ECU streams status frames while erasing, which 5am_util handles by waiting.

write.request_download_note: Byte-for-byte from 5am_util: 0x4000, then an unexplained 0x33, then the length 0x4C000.

program.note: 31 01 arms programming with the flash checksum16 appended; 33 01 executes it.

write.note: Transcribed from 5am_util main.c write_firmware(). The verbose transcript only covered reads, which is why this was 'inferred' before the source was read.

session.diagnostic_session_note: Session 0x81. The 5AM rejects 0x85 with NRC 0x22 outside the programming flow.
session.physical_evidence_note: Validated by the project capture and transcript evidence documented in PROTOCOL_NOTES.md.

ecus.notes: Sport 1100, V10 Centauro and Daytona RS. This controller uses Marelli's pre-KWP echoed one-byte diagnostic protocol, not ISO 14230 frames. memory.hardware_note: Readable on the bench: 12V on pins 4 and 17, ground on 10 and 34, K-Line on pin 16. Use a battery tender if the ECU is still on the bike.

flash.note: 0x4000-0x50000. The bootloader below 0x4000 is not reachable over K-Line. Observed directly in a 5AM HW610 dump.

eeprom.note: Holds the learned values: TPS zero, CO trim, fault memory, immobilizer codes. IAW5AMEEPROMTool covers this; the region geometry has not been captured here, so size is unset and reads will refuse rather than guess.

security.note: Seed is a 16-bit value X followed by X+1. Algorithm transcribed from 5am_util main.c calc_key() and registered as iaw5am-kwp-divmod (unverified on Guzzi hardware). See docs/PRIOR_ART.md 1.1.

session.note: 10 85 03 switches the ECU to the programming session and the line to 38400; AccessTimingParameter sets P2/P3/P4. Unlike the read path there is no 10 0C session, and the tester address stays 0xF1 (except the 27 exchange, which 5am_util sends from 0x01).

records.note: Writer identification. GuzziDiag's writer sends its TesterCode here; 5am_util sends it empty. Mandatory: RequestDownload fails without a 0x3B 98 20 record.
Reflash date, YY MM DD. 5am_util sends 2018-01-01.

erase.note: 31 02 arms the erase for 0x4000..0x4FFFF; 33 02 is what makes it run. The ECU streams status frames while erasing, which 5am_util handles by waiting.

write.request_download_note: Byte-for-byte from 5am_util: 0x4000, then an unexplained 0x33, then the length 0x4C000.

program.note: 31 01 arms programming with the flash checksum16 appended; 33 01 executes it.

write.note: Transcribed from 5am_util main.c write_firmware(). The verbose transcript only covered reads, which is why this was 'inferred' before the source was read.

session.diagnostic_session_note: Session 0x81. The 5AM rejects 0x85 with NRC 0x22 outside the programming flow.
session.physical_evidence_note: Validated by the project capture and transcript evidence documented in PROTOCOL_NOTES.md.

sim_faults.name: Head sensor, open circuit
sim_faults.description: The head temperature sensor reads the bottom rail (-40 C). The ECU fuels for a frozen engine, so it runs rich and never closes the loop.
sim_faults.teaches: A railed sensor reading, and what the rest of the channels do when the ECU believes it.

sim_faults.name: Head sensor, shorted
sim_faults.description: The head temperature sensor pins at 135 C. The ECU pulls fuelling back and the temperature lamp comes on.
sim_faults.teaches: The other rail - same sensor, opposite failure.

sim_faults.name: Throttle position sensor dead
sim_faults.description: The throttle angle stays at zero no matter what the rider does.
sim_faults.teaches: A channel that disagrees with the engine speed next to it.

sim_faults.name: Lambda sensor lazy (front)
sim_faults.description: The front sensor sits at 450 mV instead of switching. The ECU has not noticed yet and is still in closed loop.
sim_faults.teaches: What a dead narrowband sensor looks like before the ECU gives up on it - the plausibility check sees it first.

sim_faults.name: Charging system down
sim_faults.description: The alternator is not contributing. Bus voltage sits around 12.1 V and sags as the ride goes on.
sim_faults.teaches: Why every other reading drifts when the volts go away.

sim_faults.name: Air leak after the throttle
sim_faults.description: Unmetered air raises idle, the stepper closes down to compensate and both lambda integrators go positive.
sim_faults.teaches: The classic Guzzi idle complaint, with the three channels that prove it.

sim_faults.name: Idle stepper jammed
sim_faults.description: The stepper no longer moves. Idle sits well off target and the position never tracks the base.
sim_faults.teaches: Same stored code as the air leak, different fingerprint in the live data.

sim_faults.name: Front injector partially blocked
sim_faults.description: The front cylinder runs lean and its integrator climbs while the rear stays put.
sim_faults.teaches: A bank split: one map, two cylinders, very different corrections.

sim_faults.name: Rear cylinder misfire
sim_faults.description: Combustion drops out intermittently on the rear cylinder. Speed gets rough and the rear mixture goes rich with unburnt oxygen.
sim_faults.teaches: Roughness you can see in the rpm trace.

procedures.name: Idle health check
procedures.purpose: Watch the idle controller work for a few seconds and say whether it is in control. Read-only: nothing is commanded.

steps.title: Warm the engine up
steps.text: Run the engine until the head is above 70 °C and let it settle at idle. Hands off the throttle for the next step.

steps.title: Watch the idle channels
steps.text: Sampling engine speed, the ECU's idle target and the stepper.

procedures.name: Charging system check
procedures.purpose: Three voltage readings - stopped, idling and held up - which is all it takes to separate a flat battery from a dead alternator.

steps.title: Stop the engine, ignition on
steps.text: Leave the ignition on so the ECU keeps answering.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.text: Let it settle at idle before continuing.

steps.title: Hold about 3000 rpm
steps.text: Keep it steady while the next step samples.

procedures.name: Fuel pump prime and pressure decay
procedures.purpose: Prime the rail, read the gauge, wait a minute and read it again. Delivery and sealing in one test.
procedures.caveat: Pressurised fuel. Do not run this with a hot exhaust nearby.

steps.title: Fit a pressure gauge to the rail
steps.text: Engine stopped, ignition on. Fuel is about to be pressurised: no leaks, no ignition sources, catch tray down.

steps.title: Confirm the engine really is stopped
steps.text: The safety gate will not energise an output on an assumption, so the engine state is read from the ECU first.

steps.title: Prime the pump
steps.text: The workstation owns the deadline and releases the output when it expires.

steps.title: Read the gauge now
steps.text: Take the reading as soon as the pump stops.

steps.title: Wait sixty seconds
steps.text: Do not touch anything. The rail should hold its pressure.

procedures.name: Injector circuit test
procedures.purpose: Command each injector briefly with the engine stopped and confirm it answers. An electrical test, not a flow test.
procedures.caveat: Commands real injectors. Engine stopped, and mind the fuel.

steps.title: Engine stopped, ignition on
steps.text: Put your ear or a screwdriver against each injector body. Fuel pressure may be present, so expect a small squirt if a line is open.

steps.title: Confirm the engine really is stopped
steps.text: Read the engine state rather than assuming it.

procedures.name: Cold-start sensor plausibility
procedures.purpose: On a bike that has stood overnight, the head and the intake air must read nearly the same. This is the cheapest sensor test there is.

steps.title: Confirm the engine is cold
steps.text: The bike must have stood long enough to reach ambient - overnight is ideal. A warm engine makes this test meaningless.
